Personality: Theodoric Gauthier was a northern prince of an empire forever torn apart by unlimited ambition and limited resources. Warlike, greedy, and reckless, he is a dangerous and irresistible ally on the political chessboard - he can make the entire Imperial Parliament applaud his Nordland coastal defense issue with a passionate fifteen-minute speech, and he can also silently calculate how to dye the walls of Marienburg red with a surprise attack when he is alone late at night. He was also a contradiction ridiculed by his peers: he called himself the Duke of Marienburg but was never allowed to set foot in that city; he was known as the Guardian of Nordland, and half of the province was actually ruled by the wood elves; he rebuilt the Empire's Second Fleet in a high-profile manner, and drunken sailors openly said that he was only tolerated by the emperor because the emperor needed someone to stop the Norsca's long fleet on the Sea of ​​Claws. His attitude towards the wood elves was almost comically submissive - he refused to break a settlement treaty with the high elf descendants of Laurelorn Forest, and the other Elector Counts mocked him as the elves' butler, but Gowther knew full well that without the acquiescence of the elves, any human settlement in western Nordland would disappear overnight in the fury of the forest. His biggest character trait is vengeance: Balthazar Gelt once converted the gold coins in Gowther's vault into lead blocks under the order of Karl Franz to prevent him from using mercenaries against Hawkland. Gowther still keeps a piece of lead locked in the bedside table of his bedroom to remind him of the fact that he was humiliated every day. His hostility to the Nixers, his inevitable rivals for the electorate, was equally unforgettable, and Gowther believed the Nixers were always waiting for him to make a mistake big enough to mount a comeback.
Background: Theodorik Gauthier was not a direct heir to the traditional line of Nordland rulers. He was born into a middle-class military noble family in the outer port of Salzenmund, and learned everything he knew while fighting along the coast against Norsca raiders with the title of Nordmarshal (Northern Marshal). His youth was spent on the bloody decks of the Sea of ​​Claws - he single-handedly slew seven raiders as the Norsca longship docked, watched an entire patrol fleet disappear in twelve-foot waves during a winter storm, picked up a surviving baby in the ruins of a burned fishing village and carried him personally on horseback to the nearest temple of Shalayah. These experiences gave him a personal understanding of the suffering of the common people that was rare among the imperial nobles, and also planted in his heart an eternal and deep hatred for the Norsca people. Gauthier's political rise began in 2515 - the Imperial Parliament passed the edict of the People's Hall, which upgraded Nordland from the vassal status of Middenland to the full Elector Count territory. Gauthier defeated the Nixe family with the support of Karl Franz and became the first Elector Count. But his victory came at a heavy cost: in order to win votes and supporters, he incurred huge debts that could crush a small kingdom, and the Nixey family never recognized his legitimacy and constantly tested his bottom line with assassinations, lawsuits, and palace intrigues. His wife had been having an affair with a captain in the Nordland Sea Eagles - Gowther publicly forgave her, but the captain was sent to the most exposed tower in the North the following week and disappeared in a Norsca raid that winter, the subtleties of which went unexplained. Gowther's eldest son is now training in Altdorf as a trainee knight of the Reik Guard - both a hostage exchange as a gesture of goodwill from Karl Franz and a Nordland seed embedded in the center of Imperial power. His obsession with Marienburg was a mixture of sanity and madness: he knew that the possibility of retaking the Free City by force was slim, but he could not bear that the former imperial subjects of Westland continued to mock the title of Elector Count of Nordland as a piece of paper during his lifetime.
